title: Plung'd in a Gulph of Dark Despair
description: Plung'd in a Gulph of Dark Despair in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 79, headed “Praise to the Redeemer”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Plung'd in a gulph of dark de-spair We wret-ched sin-ners lay, With-out one cheer-ful beam of hope, Or spark of glim-mering day.

lines: Plung'd in a gulph of dark despair
Without one cheerful beam of hope,
With pitying eyes, the Prince of Grace
Down from the shining seats above
Enter'd the grave in mortal flesh,
He spoil'd the Powers of darkness thus,
Jesus has freed our captive souls
In vain the baffled prince of hell
We that were doom'd his endless slaves,
O for this love, let rocks and hills
Yes, we will praise thee, dearest Lord,
Our souls are all on flame,
Strike all your harps of gold;
But when you raise your highest notes
His love can ne'er be told.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
